correctness.rationale: For any support with at most two coordinates, the two equations and distinct λ force all coordinates zero. Hence a single fixes precisely its smooth anticanonical elliptic section, while a double fixes exactly the four reduced intersections of two conics in the complementary plane. At an isolated fixed point of a double, the tangent action is −I; along a single's fixed curve it is a reflection. Two singles meet in four points with independent reflection directions, so even their full stabilizer gives smooth quotient points. In the mixed group, the double supports are complementary pairs among the four indices other than the single. Their fixed sets are disjoint from one another and from the single fixed section. In an all-double group the three supports are the edges of a triangle, and pairwise fixed-set intersections would leave at most two nonzero coordinates. Thus the latter two rows have 8/2 and 12/2 isolated stabilizer orbits of local type A1. Two singles give 10 subgroups; choosing a single and one of the six disjoint doubles gives 5·6/2=15 mixed subgroups; the all-double groups are the 10 triangles. The count is exhaustive since (15·14)/(3·2)=35. Hurwitz gives pullback of −K equal to (1+r) times the hyperplane class for r single flips, hence degree (1+r)²; Cartierness follows from smooth or A1 local models, and ampleness descends. For topology, the two-single quotient is P² (one can eliminate both squared coordinates in the invariant ring). In the middle row first quotient by the single: elimination of its square leaves a smooth quadric P1×P1, with the residual involution fixing precisely four points, the orbits of the double fixed sets. Removing these points leaves the simply connected topological double cover of the quotient smooth locus. For the all-double groups, removing twelve points from the simply connected quartic surface gives the simply connected degree-four free cover; normalization extends it uniquely to X. A precision in frozen proof step 4: U must mean the exact preimage of Y^sm, not X minus every point fixed by a double, since the double in the first row also fixes four points with reflection-generated full stabilizers and smooth images. The independent staged proof above verifies the original groups without that identification. For the weighted equation, parity of the three flipped coordinates gives exactly the square generators and v, and exactness of invariants in characteristic zero allows elimination by the two invariant quadrics. The coefficient matrix has determinant λ1−λ0; solving gives the displayed L0,L1. Each pair of branch sections reduces on [s:t] to αs²+βt²=0 with α,β nonzero differences of λ's, so has two transverse crossings; any triple would force s=t=u=0. The sextic is smooth over the weighted base vertex (on the u=1 cover v is nonzero and the residual sign action exchanges the two lifts). Thus the three listed components are the divisorial branch, and there is no extra quotient singularity there. The frozen checker enumerates groups; its printed geometry fields are not independent geometric proof.

originality.rationale: The original sign group and fixed-locus types, the two-reflection quotient degree, and the all-double six-node degree-one example with its covering implication are substantially prior. The generic weighted-sextic format is classical. The supported distinct content is the exact complete profile for the canonical sign family, in particular the one-reflection subgroup's ordinary quotient and smooth-locus covering profile in the census, together with the explicit eigenvalue-dependent factorized equation. No first-claim attribution is made for the known end rows or general covering methods.
residual_risks: Existing classification tables for Gorenstein log del Pezzo surfaces might give individual baskets or universal covers under other descriptions; the bounded search does not certify the uniqueness of the combined profile.
The standard weighted embedding and exact six-node all-double example do not independently support priority.

value.rationale: For the canonical sign action, enumerating the 35 subgroups is easy but does not itself distinguish divisorial-branch stabilizers from isolated inertia or determine smooth-locus covers. The complete natural classification connects the mixed row and both end cases to exact subgroup multiplicities and gives a concrete model of the all-double stratum. This is useful as a specific quotient-and-cover reference, not a new general classification of log del Pezzo surfaces or evidence that 35 quotient isomorphism classes occur.
